AI & Data Systems for Emergency Operations

I build the AI agents, data pipelines, and analytics platforms that Amazon's Global Security Operations Center relies on to detect, classify, and respond to real-world safety incidents affecting drivers and worksites. As a Certified Risk Management Professional (CRMP — DRI International), I bring formal business-continuity and disaster-recovery discipline to how I design these systems — building them to fail safely, stay accurate under pressure, and keep the right signal reaching decision-makers when a real emergency is unfolding. Pairing that risk-and-resilience foundation with modern AI (Amazon Bedrock, agentic automation) is what lets me turn fragmented, high-stakes operational data into reproducible, decision-grade intelligence leaders can trust. MBA in Business Analytics (STEM) and 6+ years delivering to senior stakeholders.

Dashboards · Data Engineering

Balance Scorecard 4.0 Sole Developer

Problem

GSOC had no centralized analytics — a manual weekly Excel process distributed 2–3 days after period close.

What I Built

GSOC's unified QuickSight platform: six role-based views with Row-Level Security. I modeled 6 Redshift sources into a single source of truth, normalizing 900+ raw fields into 84 governed KPIs and cutting a core query from 810s to 35s.

Impact

Serves 200+ agents through VP-level leadership across three global regions; 88% legacy match, 99%+ on core metrics; 10+ analyst hrs/week saved.

Platform Highlights
  • Live hourly KPI command center — OTR/UTR, total calls, incident rooms, EMT notifications/created/pending, out-of-scope EMTs, per-language volumes, calls/hr vs. prior hour, emails & outbound, each with week-over-week deltas and a built-in Q&A chat.
  • Sankey call-flow analysis — end-to-end LMET routing (calls → OTR/UTR language queues → live agents → transfer destinations) and a SONNI OTR bot flow showing contained vs. transferred vs. live-agent vs. abandoned.
  • Workforce & shift analytics — Watch Commanders, shifts, directs and total workforce; SWA %, agent answer rate, IPH, and calls-per-hour broken down by shift.
  • Leadership radar views — Watch-Commander × team comparisons across productive time, answer rate, phone availability, email %, incident/hr, and high-sev & mitigation calls.
  • Real-time trends — inbound volume per hour and call volume per language vs. agents staffed.
  • Netradyne callback analysis — callback-volume trend plus a per-contact detail table (queue wait, disconnect reason, EMT-notification rate).
